subject: Accelerated invoice lane request + PO reconciliation
messages:
From: Alice Sullivan <alice.sullivan@horizonhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@horizonhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-17T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Request: accelerated invoice cadence + PO ID reconciliation

Hi Vivek,

Quick ask from procurement — we can get Redwood into our AP system if invoices include the Horizon PO ID on every line item and if we can move the first three invoices to a weekly/accelerated lane for the initial onboarding month. Our standard supplier terms are net45, but onboarding requires we see actual invoices processed within 30 days to complete vendor validation.

Specifics:
- PO: 77821 (attached) — please confirm you can map this to your invoices.
- Invoice cadence: can you run the first 3 invoices on an accelerated weekly/payment-run cadence?
- Holdback: procurement may need to hold back a portion (~20-30%) of the onboarding month until acceptance testing is complete.

Also flagging that we need a single consolidated invoice file that our AP team can ingest (CSV preferred).

Can you confirm feasibility and any commercial implications?

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Sullivan
Sr. Manager, Procurement
Horizon Health

[Attachment: Horizon_PO_77821.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alice Sullivan <alice.sullivan@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: accelerated invoice cadence + PO ID reconciliation

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear note and the PO. We can absolutely include the Horizon PO ID on every invoice line and provide a CSV export your AP team can ingest. A couple of clarifying questions on the commercial side before I lock down the plan:

1) Accelerated cadence impact: running the first three invoices on an accelerated lane increases short-term processing/routing overhead on our side. For that we typically ask for either a small onboarding surcharge or a temporary change to prepay/holdback terms.
2) Holdback mechanics: how long is the holdback expected to stay in place once acceptance testing is complete?
3) Net terms: Horizon referenced net45 as the standard — are you requesting we invoice immediately but accept the holdback, or do you want net30 for these first invoices?

Proposed options from our side (we're flexible):
- Option A (preferred): Accelerated weekly run x3, keep net45, 25% onboarding holdback released within 10 business days of acceptance sign-off. No change to list price.
- Option B: Accelerated weekly run x3, move to net30 for first 60 days in exchange for a one-time 2% onboarding credit/discount.

I've looped Marissa and Ben to weigh in on commercial and finance feasibility; will follow up with a firm write-up once we agree internally.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T08:32:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: accelerated invoice cadence + PO ID reconciliation (pricing options)

Team — forwarding Horizon's ask and my reply. Need quick internal alignment so I can get a clean response to procurement today. Key constraints: they need PO on every line (easy), accelerated first 3 invoices (operational), and a 20-30% holdback.

Quick thoughts:
- Finance impact: accelerated runs mean we front consumable processing costs; I recommend Option A (no list-price change, 25% holdback) to keep margin intact. We absorb ops cost for first 3 runs.
- If procurement insists on net30 rather than net45, we should ask for a 2% onboarding credit — low impact but keeps cashflow stable.
- We should provide the CSV template (attached) to avoid follow-ups and reduce AP friction.

If we do Option A, we need finance sign-off on the 25% holdback release timeline. Ben — can you confirm this is acceptable operationally and whether a 25% holdback is feasible to reconcile? Lauren — any concerns from pricing/renewal side about setting a precedent?

Thanks — aiming to get a succinct reply to Alice by EOD.

Vivek

[Attachment: redwood_invoice_template_v2.csv (text/csv)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alice Sullivan <alice.sullivan@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: accelerated invoice cadence + PO ID reconciliation

Hi Alice — thanks for the quick turnaround. We reviewed internally and can support Horizon's onboarding requirements with the plan below. Please confirm acceptance so we can issue the first accelerated invoice this week.

Agreed plan (summary):
- PO mapping: Redwood will include PO 77821 on every invoice line item and in the CSV export.
- Accelerated invoice lane: Redwood will run the first 3 invoices on an accelerated weekly cadence (one run per week) to support your vendor validation process.
- Holdback: Horizon may hold back 25% of each onboarding invoice. Redwood requests that holdback portion be released within 10 business days of Horizon's acceptance sign-off for onboarding milestones.
- Net terms and discount: We will keep Horizon on net45. If Horizon requires net30 for onboarding, Redwood requests a 2% one-time onboarding credit to offset cashflow impact. Please indicate preference.
- Deliverables: attached CSV invoice template and a short amendment (DocuSign link) that formalizes the accelerated lane and holdback mechanics.

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether Horizon wants net45 (preferred) or net30 + 2% credit.
2) If acceptable, sign the amendment via DocuSign and return the first PO-mapped invoice CSV.

I've attached the CSV template and a draft amendment. If you prefer, we can apply the net30 + 2% credit approach immediately; just let me know and we'll reflect that in the amendment before signature.

Best regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
